invariants_created: Server sends 220 banner upon connection before any client command is accepted
EHLO or HELO MUST be the first client command issued after receiving the 220 banner
EHLO or HELO MUST precede MAIL FROM
MAIL FROM MUST precede RCPT TO
RCPT TO MUST precede DATA
At least one successful RCPT TO is required before DATA
AUTH must follow EHLO (not HELO); AUTH is not valid after HELO
STARTTLS must follow EHLO and must precede both AUTH and MAIL FROM
RSET returns the session to the post-greeting (GREETED) state without closing the connection, allowing a new MAIL FROM to be issued
RCPT TO can be issued multiple times after a single MAIL FROM to specify multiple recipients
After DATA content is transmitted and terminated with '.', the session returns to GREETED state allowing a new MAIL FROM for another transaction
NOOP and VRFY can be issued at any point during the session without affecting the transaction state
After RSET, a new MAIL FROM can be issued to start a fresh transaction within the same session
QUIT should be the last command issued; server responds 221 and closes the connection
EHLO.hostname: Required. Must be a valid hostname or FQDN. Cannot be empty.
HELO.hostname: Required. Must be a valid hostname or FQDN. Cannot be empty.
MAIL.sender: Required. Must be enclosed in angle brackets (e.g., <sender@domain>). May be <> (null reverse-path) for bounce/delivery-status messages. Must include the 'FROM:' keyword.
RCPT.recipient: Required. Must be enclosed in angle brackets (e.g., <recipient@domain>). Must include the 'TO:' keyword. At least one RCPT TO with a 250 response is required before DATA.

DATA.body: Message content must follow the 354 server response. Content consists of RFC 5322 headers, a blank line, and the message body. Must be terminated by a line containing only a single period (.). Lines starting with a period in the original content must be dot-stuffed (prepend an extra period).
AUTH.mechanism: Required. Must be one of the SASL mechanisms advertised by the server in the EHLO response (commonly PLAIN, LOGIN, or CRAM-MD5). AUTH is only valid after EHLO, not after HELO.
AUTH.initial-response: Optional. Base64-encoded initial authentication data. Depends on the SASL mechanism in use.
VRFY.address: Required. A mailbox address to verify. Often disabled by servers for security/privacy reasons.
EXPN.list: Required. A mailing list name to expand. Often disabled by servers for security/privacy reasons.

RCPT.count: At least one RCPT TO must be issued and accepted (250 response) before DATA. Multiple RCPT TO commands are permitted per MAIL FROM transaction. A 550 response for a recipient does not prevent other recipients from being accepted.
MAIL.precedence: Must be preceded by EHLO or HELO. Cannot be issued before a successful greeting.
STARTTLS.precedence: Must be preceded by EHLO. Must precede AUTH and MAIL FROM. After successful STARTTLS, client must re-issue EHLO over the encrypted channel.

status_changes.description: CONNECTED -> GREETED via EHLO
status_changes.rationale: Evidence is only heuristic trace augmentation — no direct observed trace or probe data confirms this transition actually occurred. The transition is plausible per SMTP protocol but remains unverified by concrete behavioral evidence.

status_changes.description: CONNECTED -> GREETED via HELO
status_changes.rationale: Same as EHLO variant: only heuristic trace augmentation evidence. Plausible per RFC 5321 but no direct trace or probe confirmation.

status_changes.description: GREETED -> MAIL_PENDING via MAIL
status_changes.rationale: Heuristic trace augmentation only. No observed trace or probe data to confirm the state transition actually occurs in practice.

status_changes.description: AUTHENTICATED -> MAIL_PENDING via MAIL
status_changes.rationale: Heuristic trace augmentation only. No direct behavioral evidence; the AUTHENTICATED state and its transitions are inferred, not observed.

status_changes.description: MAIL_PENDING -> RCPT_PENDING via RCPT
status_changes.rationale: Heuristic trace augmentation only. Plausible per SMTP but unverified by direct trace or probe evidence.

status_changes.description: RCPT_PENDING -> RCPT_PENDING via RCPT
status_changes.rationale: Heuristic trace augmentation only. The self-loop on RCPT_PENDING for additional recipients is plausible but unverified by observed behavior.

status_changes.description: RCPT_PENDING -> DATA_PENDING via DATA
status_changes.rationale: Heuristic trace augmentation only. No direct trace or probe evidence confirms this transition.

status_changes.description: MAIL_PENDING -> GREETED via RSET
status_changes.rationale: Heuristic trace augmentation only. RSET returning to GREETED is plausible per RFC but unverified by concrete evidence.

status_changes.description: RCPT_PENDING -> GREETED via RSET
status_changes.rationale: Heuristic trace augmentation only. Same concern as MAIL_PENDING -> GREETED via RSET; no observed trace confirmation.

status_changes.description: GREETED -> CLOSED via QUIT
status_changes.rationale: Heuristic trace augmentation only. Plausible per SMTP QUIT semantics but no direct trace or probe evidence.

status_changes.description: Server sends 220 banner upon connection before any client command is accepted
status_changes.rationale: Evidence is solely from LLM Spec Agent documentation — no direct trace or probe observation of a 220 banner being sent. Well-known SMTP behavior but unverified by concrete behavioral data.

status_changes.description: EHLO or HELO MUST be the first client command issued after receiving the 220 banner
status_changes.rationale: Doc-only evidence from LLM Spec Agent. No trace data showing a server rejecting a non-EHLO/HELO first command. Plausible per RFC but unverified.

status_changes.description: EHLO or HELO MUST precede MAIL FROM
status_changes.rationale: Doc-only evidence. No observed trace showing server enforcement of this ordering constraint.

status_changes.description: MAIL FROM MUST precede RCPT TO
status_changes.rationale: Doc-only evidence. No trace or probe data confirming server rejection of RCPT TO before MAIL FROM.

status_changes.description: RCPT TO MUST precede DATA
status_changes.rationale: Doc-only evidence. No observed trace confirming server enforcement of this ordering.

status_changes.description: At least one successful RCPT TO is required before DATA
status_changes.rationale: Doc-only evidence. No trace showing a server rejecting DATA when no successful RCPT TO has been issued.

status_changes.description: AUTH must follow EHLO (not HELO); AUTH is not valid after HELO
status_changes.rationale: Doc-only evidence. No trace or probe showing AUTH being rejected after HELO or accepted after EHLO.

status_changes.description: STARTTLS must follow EHLO and must precede both AUTH and MAIL FROM
status_changes.rationale: Doc-only evidence. No observed trace confirming STARTTLS ordering enforcement by the server.

status_changes.description: RSET returns the session to the post-greeting (GREETED) state without closing the connection, allowing a new MAIL FROM to be issued
status_changes.rationale: Doc-only evidence. No trace showing RSET behavior and resulting state. Plausible per RFC but unverified.

status_changes.description: RCPT TO can be issued multiple times after a single MAIL FROM to specify multiple recipients
status_changes.rationale: Doc-only evidence. No observed trace confirming multiple RCPT TO commands being accepted in a single transaction.

status_changes.description: After DATA content is transmitted and terminated with '.', the session returns to GREETED state allowing a new MAIL FROM for another transaction
status_changes.rationale: Doc-only evidence. No trace confirming the state transition after DATA termination. The transition model is plausible but unverified.

status_changes.description: NOOP and VRFY can be issued at any point during the session without affecting the transaction state
status_changes.rationale: Doc evidence includes example session traces (Session 4 and Session 9) showing NOOP/VRFY interleaving, which provides slightly more concrete support than pure specification claims. However, these are still LLM-generated examples, not observed traces.

status_changes.description: After RSET, a new MAIL FROM can be issued to start a fresh transaction within the same session
status_changes.rationale: Doc evidence includes example session traces (Session 3 and Session 10) showing RSET followed by new MAIL FROM, providing slightly more concrete support. Still LLM-generated examples rather than observed traces.

status_changes.description: QUIT should be the last command issued; server responds 221 and closes the connection
status_changes.rationale: Doc-only evidence. No observed trace confirming 221 response and connection closure after QUIT.
